newsitem.title: LUXEMBOURG: Court finds Community tax rules on re-exported goods valid.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Community tax rules on re-exported goods valid.

text.p: The European Court of Justice found no reason on Thursday to alter the current system of inward processing relief for cane and beet sugars under Community regulations.

The French-based sugar producer Eridania Beghin-Say SA imported raw sugar cane from Cuba under the inward processing relief tax scheme. It then exported processed sugar, which was made in part from the imported cane, but also included some beet sugar.

The French taxing authorities said Eridania could not suspend import duties on the processed sugar, because beet sugar does not fall into the same tax category as cane sugar in the Community regulations and therefore does not qualify for the same exemption.
Eridania argued that the Community rules violate general principles of proportionality, and legitimate expectations and legal certainty.
The court disagreed and found Council regulation No 3677/86 valid and unchanged by Eridania's arguments.
